title: Rust crate
confidence_notes: Cargo.toml at the root is necessary, not sufficient. A workspace root with only [workspace] and no [package] is still rust-crate at lower confidence; pick the member with a bench/ or the largest src/. If Cargo.toml lists axum, actix-web, tonic, hyper or warp and there is a main.rs that binds a port, add service-api. If there is a [[bin]] and a clap/argh dependency but no server, add cli-tool. A crate whose src/ is mostly generated bindings (bindgen, prost) has almost no honest algorithmic headroom; say so in the profile.

default_cards.title: Failing tests (unit + integration + doctests)

measure.command: out=$(cargo test 2>&1); rc=$?; f=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/^test result:/{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="failed;") n+=$(i-1)} END{print n+0}'); [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$f" -eq 0 ] && f=1; echo "METRIC tests_failed=$f"

gaming_risks: a test module deleted, #[ignore]d, or gated behind a cfg the runner never enables
assertions weakened or wrapped in a Result that is never checked
a failing test's body replaced by a trivially passing one in a non-frozen path
cargo test filtered via .cargo/config.toml aliases or an env var so the failing test is never collected
build failure reads as one failure: a run that compiles nothing is not a pass

default_cards.title: Clippy warnings, all targets

measure.command: out=$(cargo clippy --all-targets --message-format=short 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; exit 1; }; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/^[^ ]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+: warning:/{n++} END{print "METRIC clippy_warnings=" n+0}'

degradation.apply: printf '\npub fn sb_degradation(v: &Vec<u8>) -> usize { v.len() }\n' >> src/lib.rs

gaming_risks: #![allow(clippy::...)] or #[allow] attributes added to silence rather than fix
clippy.toml thresholds raised (protected path, but check the diff for an inline equivalent)
a warning-heavy module moved behind a cfg that --all-targets does not enable
lint level demoted in Cargo.toml [lints] table

default_cards.title: Release compile time of this crate, deps cached

degradation.apply: python3 -c "print('\n'.join('pub fn sb_bloat_%d(x: u64) -> u64 { let mut v: Vec<u64> = (0..x).collect(); v.sort_unstable(); v.iter().map(|y| y.wrapping_mul(%d)).sum() }' % (i, i + 1) for i in range(3000)))" >> src/lib.rs

gaming_risks: code deleted or moved into a dependency crate that cargo clean -p does not touch, so it is measured as cached
opt-level or codegen-units lowered in Cargo.toml [profile.release] (that is a config-operator change and must be declared as one)
generic code replaced by dyn dispatch that compiles faster but is slower at runtime: check the bench guardrail moved
features disabled so less of the crate compiles
a proc-macro or build.rs made lazy in a way that skips work only when SB_* env vars are present

default_cards.title: Release binary size

measure.command: cargo build --release --message-format=json-render-diagnostics 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import json,sys,os; p=[m.get("executable") for m in map(json.loads, sys.stdin) if m.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and m.get("executable")]; print("METRIC binary_bytes=%d" % os.path.getsize(p[-1]))'

gaming_risks: strip = true, lto, opt-level = "z" or panic = "abort" set in [profile.release]: legitimate only as a declared config hypothesis, and panic=abort changes semantics
features or whole subcommands removed
debug info stripped while the profile said it should be kept
the measured binary swapped for a smaller [[bin]] target: the parser takes the last artifact, so check which executable was built
a large table moved from the binary into a file read at runtime

default_cards.title: Criterion bench {{bench_filter}}, ns per iteration
gaming_risks: the hot function special-cases the fixture's size, shape, or a sentinel value the bench supplies
a result cache keyed on the exact input the bench passes, warm on the second iteration
work deferred out of the measured closure (lazy evaluation that the bench never forces)
black_box removed or the bench's input built once outside the loop in a non-frozen helper
SIMD or unsafe fast path only correct for the fixture's alignment; correctness lives in the tests guardrail, check it ran
the bench reads SB_SEED: if it does not, the holdout is a no-op and the metrologist must switch to a dir holdout

default_cards.title: Occurrences of the unsafe keyword under src/

degradation.apply: printf '\npub fn sb_degradation() -> u8 { unsafe { *(&7u8 as *const u8) } }\n' >> src/lib.rs

gaming_risks: unsafe moved into a dependency crate, a macro, or a file outside src/
one big unsafe block replacing several small ones (count falls, exposure rises): read the diff, not the number
the word hidden behind a macro_rules! that expands to unsafe

default_cards.title: Public API items (cargo public-api)

measure.command: command -v cargo-public-api >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 3; cargo public-api --simplified 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^pub '

gaming_risks: an item made pub(crate) or #[doc(hidden)] to keep the count while breaking downstream users
one item removed and one added so the count is unchanged: an equal count is necessary, not sufficient; the recommended check is cargo public-api diff against the baseline commit
a type's fields changed from pub to private (count of items can stay the same)

default_cards.title: Builds on the minimum supported Rust version

measure.command: rustup run {{msrv}} rustc --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 3; if cargo +{{msrv}} check --quiet --all-targets 2>/dev/null; then echo METRIC msrv_build_failed=0; else echo METRIC msrv_build_failed=1; fi

degradation.apply: printf '\npub fn sb_degradation_msrv() -> u32 { let v = [1u32, 2, 3]; v.iter().map(|x| x.isqrt()).sum() }\n' >> src/lib.rs

gaming_risks: rust-version in Cargo.toml raised (protected via Cargo.toml review, not a frozen path: read the diff)
the failing code moved behind a feature the MSRV check does not enable

noise_sources: CPU frequency scaling and thermal throttling on laptops
shared target/ directory between worktrees: a warm dep cache is intended, a warm crate cache is not (cargo clean -p before timing)
criterion's own outlier handling hides multimodal timings; read the bencher line, not the summary
background cargo processes from another worktree (measurement must be serialized)
notes: Reuse before inventing: if benches/ exists, every criterion group is a candidate bench_ns card; one card per group, filter by group name. Fill {{crate_name}} from [package].name, {{bench_name}} from [[bench]] or the file stem under benches/, {{bench_filter}} from the criterion function id as printed by --output-format bencher. binary_bytes needs a [[bin]] target; for a library-only crate replace the parser with the .rlib path from the same json stream (filenames[0]). build_release_s and bench_ns are contention_safe=false and must be measured serially; CARGO_TARGET_DIR is shared across worktrees by the harness, which is why the compile-time card runs cargo clean -p first. public_api_items needs cargo-public-api and a nightly toolchain for rustdoc JSON; if absent the command exits 3 and the card is quarantined rather than reading zero. The MSRV card needs the toolchain installed; read {{msrv}} from [package].rust-version. The equal-direction guardrail treats any change as worse for the degradation probe. Compile time plus binary size with clippy and public_api_items as guardrails is the canonical first campaign for a crate without benches.
